newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said an inspection mission to the UK had confirmed Commission suspicions that British beef had been illegally exported to several member states and third countries despite the ban established in March 1996 in the framework of the fight against BSE.
Despite repeated questions the Commission did not give any figures on the quantity of beef involved or name the countries concerned.
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission did not want to hinder several police and court inquiries already begun in this matter.
Vale de Almeida said the Commission was disappointed that an agreement on restrictions on imports could not have been reached between the EU and India.

Vale de Almeida said the Commission had discussed unwrapped non-food articles mixed with food-products during its weekly meeting. He said legislation existed in all member states but that it was not applied rigorously enough.
Vale de Almeida said Commissioner Hans van den Broek would not attend a new donor conference on Bosnia if the Bosnian authorities did not reach an agreement with the International Monetary Fund.
Van der Pas said the Commission had not reached a decision on Italian aid to Thomson/SGS.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/593: The impact of the euro on the capital markets.
- IP/97/595: Commission provides financial support to the Human Rights Ombudsperson for Bosnia Herzegovina.
- IP/97/596: EU is the largest donor to Bosnia Herzegovina - Commission will only participate in new donor conference after IMF agreement.
- IP/97/597: Commission opens state aid procedure against Everts Erfurt GmbH, Thuringia.
- IP/97/598: State aid: The Netherlands - Commission approves the cost allocuation rules of NedCar motor vehicles.
- IP/97/600: EU disappointed at outcome of talks on India's import restrictions.
